claims.text: A TaNbHfZrTi-type refractory high-entropy alloy can enhance catalytic activity toward both HER and HOR.
The proposed refractory high-entropy alloy can provide long-term durability during HER and HOR.
Interstitial O or N doping can tune the alloy's surface electronic structure.
Interstitial O or N doping can stabilize active sites against corrosion.
The initial TaNbHfZrTi-type alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Controlled O or N doping may produce ordered interstitial complexes in the alloy.
Introducing controlled O or N interstitial doping during processing will form ordered interstitial complexes.
Introducing controlled interstitial doping will refine the surface microstructure.
Surface ordered interstitial complexes and a nanostructured BCC matrix modify the d-band electronic structure of transition-metal sites.
Interstitial doping adjusts the electronic properties of the multi-metal surface atoms.
The electronic changes caused by interstitial doping lower the activation energy for hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
Interstitial doping improves resistance to corrosion and mechanical degradation.
Synergy among several refractory metals and interstitial stabilizers enhances catalytic kinetics.
Synergy among several refractory metals and interstitial stabilizers improves durability under aggressive reaction conditions.
The alloy electrode will have lower HER and HOR overpotentials than conventional Pt-based catalysts under comparable conditions.
The alloy electrode will have more favorable HER and HOR Tafel slopes than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The alloy electrode will maintain stable catalytic performance over prolonged electrochemical cycling.
Potential surface segregation or changes in electrochemical environment may prevent the proposed surface stabilization and d-band tuning.
No direct catalytic testing evidence is available in the cited references for the proposed alloy's HER or HOR performance.
